normalization.title: The Best Model Shouldn't Do Every Job
normalization.overview: AI LABS walks through nine rules for Claude Fable 5.2, beginning with when *not* to use it. The 16-minute video compares Fable with Opus 5.5, explains finish-line tests and lead/worker delegation, then covers effort, unattended permissions, reporting, instruction audits and model switching. It is a practical workflow guide, not a controlled scientific comparison.
normalization.whyItMatters: If you use coding agents on meaningful projects, the expensive mistake is not merely paying for too many tokens. It is picking the wrong model, handing off work without a definition of done, or accepting an agent's completion claim without evidence. Watch the routing and delegation sections at 03:52–09:50. The later operating rules are useful if you supervise longer runs. You can skip the 09:50–10:51 sponsor segment. Verify the claimed cost experiments independently before using them for budget decisions.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Optimize for a verified, accountable job rather than the prestige or per-token price of a model. Begin with sufficient capability, escalate selectively, delegate only work that can be checked, and distinguish technical permissions from owner authorization. That is an editorial design rule, not proof that a particular multiagent setup will always save money.
